title: Normalized constant-coefficient models on presented topoi
statement: Use fixed small-site presentations of Grothendieck topoi [def-weil-pbc-topos], the existing categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A presentation records its site, topology and the usual small-site sheafification instances. For a commutative ring R, its coefficient ring sheaf is the sheafification of the constant presheaf R. Write Mod_R(W), D_R(W), and |-| for its module category, derived category and underlying-set-sheaf functor. For a unital map phi:A→B, take a normalized scalar model [def-weil-pbc-system-scalar-model] for the induced constant-ring map; write S_W for its derived tensor functor, the derived functor of its derived change-of-rings cochain model [def-sfb-derived-change-of-rings-cochain-model] and U_W for exact derived restriction of scalars. For a geometric morphism g:T→W [def-trf-geometric-morphism], an inverse model is an algebraic inverse-image presentation [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image] over the constant R-sheaves, additive and exact. Its ring identification carries each constant r to r using the terminal constant sheaf, and its derived inverse is the exact induced functor. A direct model is a right adjoint to that derived inverse, with its adjunction; its adjunction determines the derived direct image up to unique counit-compatible isomorphism. For inverse models L_A,L_B, a scalar/pullback presentation consists of an ordinary restriction/inverse-image isomorphism U_W L_A≅L_B U_T which is the identity under the underlying-sheaf identifications, and an isomorphism lambda:L_B S_W≅S_T L_A whose inverse has that exact descended restriction comparison as scalar-adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. A vertex consists of W, a second presentation Wtilde, a comparison geometric morphism nu:Wtilde→W, both inverse models N_A,N_B, both scalar models and this normalized scalar/pullback comparison. All functors and identifications are retained as data, without assuming a mixed derived cube or faithfulness of a derived forgetful functor.
